body.name: retained empirical bootstrap
body.construction: Choose a deterministic sequence \(B_n\to\infty\). Conditional on the original sample, generate exactly \(B_n\) mutually independent Efron \(n\)-out-of-\(n\) candidate samples using \(I_{bj}^{*}\), center each resample by its own mean, and compute \(\widehat\delta_{n,b}^{*}\) and \(\widehat\Theta_{n,b}^{*,\mathrm{tot}}\) with the same ridge map \(R_n\). Retain candidate \(b\) exactly when \(J_{n,b}=\mathbf 1\{\widehat\delta_{n,b}^{*}>0\}=1\). If \(M_n>0\), output the empirical endpoint-pair law \(\widehat{\mathbb L}_n^{\mathrm{ret}}\) over the retained draws and its left-continuous coordinate quantiles \(Q_{n,-}^{\mathrm{ret}}\) and \(Q_{n,+}^{\mathrm{ret}}\). If \(M_n=0\), output the Dirac law at the original totalized endpoint pair. This is a finite Monte Carlo realization of Watson et al.'s Theorem 4 feasibility filter and the \(p=2\) \(\texttt{leakyIV}\) branch; it is measurable on every original sample and every candidate resample.
